record.paper_title: Results and Open Questions on the Boundary Control of Moving Sets
record.original_question: For the optimal set motion problem (OSM), Theorem 4.1 gives existence of optimal solutions in a very general class of sets with finite perimeter, while the Pontryagin-type necessary conditions in Section 5 require much stronger regularity. Prove regularity of an optimal set-valued map t→Ω(t) solving (OSM) that is strong enough to justify those necessary conditions; in particular, prove that the orthogonal trajectories to the moving boundaries ∂Ω(t) are well defined.

evidence.quote: At this stage, we must point out that a major gap still remains in the theory. Indeed, Theorem 4.1 yields the existence of optimal solutions t 7→ Ω(t) within a general class of sets with finite perimeter. On the other hand, the necessary conditions require a much stronger regularity assumption.
Problem 2. Establish the regularity of the set valued map t 7→ Ω(t) which provides a solution to (OSM). In particular, prove that the orthogonal curves to the boundaries ∂Ω(t) are well defined.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $T>0$ and consider a time-dependent family of bounded sets of finite perimeter $\{\Omega(t)\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, modeling the spread of a contaminating region. Given an initial set $\Omega_0\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of finite perimeter and a constant $c>0$ representing the maximal outward propagation speed of the uncontrolled front, admissible motions are set-valued maps $t\mapsto\Omega(t)$ such that $\Omega(0)=\Omega_0$ and the boundary $\partial\Omega(t)$ moves outward with normal velocity at most $c$, except along a controlled portion $\Gamma(t)\subseteq\partial\Omega(t)$ where the boundary is held fixed (or pushed inward) by a control effort. The total length of the controlled portion at time $t$ is bounded by a prescribed function $M(t)$, i.e.\ $\mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma(t))\le M(t)$.

The optimal set motion problem (OSM) is
$$\min_{t\mapsto\Omega(t)}\ \int_0^T \big[\,|\Omega(t)|+\alpha\,\mathcal{H}^1(\Gamma(t))\,\big]\,dt + \beta\,|\Omega(T)|,$$
for fixed constants $\alpha,\beta\ge 0$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes Lebesgue measure and $\mathcal{H}^1$ is the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, and the minimization is taken over admissible motions as above.

It is known that (OSM) admits an optimal solution in the class of motions $t\mapsto\Omega(t)$ for which each $\Omega(t)$ has finite perimeter. On the other hand, the Pontryagin-type necessary conditions for optimality require much stronger regularity, in particular the existence of well-defined orthogonal trajectories to the moving boundaries $\partial\Omega(t)$, $t\in[0,T]$.

Problem. Prove that every optimal solution $t\mapsto\Omega(t)$ of (OSM) enjoys regularity strong enough to justify the Pontryagin-type necessary conditions. In particular, show that for almost every point $x_0\in\partial\Omega(t_0)$ (with $t_0\in(0,T)$) there exists a unique Lipschitz curve $s\mapsto\gamma(s)$, defined on a neighborhood of $t_0$, such that $\gamma(t_0)=x_0$, $\gamma(s)\in\partial\Omega(s)$ for each $s$, and $\dot\gamma(s)$ is orthogonal to $\partial\Omega(s)$ at $\gamma(s)$; that is, the orthogonal trajectories to the moving boundaries $\partial\Omega(t)$ are well defined.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question in Bressan's 2025 survey on boundary control of moving sets, where it is stated that a major gap remains between existence of optimal solutions in the class of finite-perimeter sets and the much stronger regularity required to justify the Pontryagin-type necessary conditions. No subsequent work resolving the regularity of the optimal set-valued map and the well-posedness of orthogonal trajectories to the moving boundaries was found.

status_evidence.title: Results and Open Questions on the Boundary Control of Moving Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 4.1 yields existence of optimal solutions in a general class of finite-perimeter sets, while the necessary conditions require much stronger regularity; establishing regularity of t↦Ω(t) and well-defined orthogonal curves to ∂Ω(t) is listed as Problem 2.
status_evidence.claim: The regularity question is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Control of Moving Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of optimal sets with finite perimeter and necessary conditions assuming smoother boundaries are derived, but the matching regularity theory bridging these two settings is not established.
status_evidence.claim: Companion work establishes existence and necessary conditions separately, leaving regularity open.

status_evidence.title: On the Regularity of Optimal Dynamic Blocking Strategies
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity is studied for related dynamic blocking problems but does not resolve the regularity for the (OSM) formulation in the survey.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct regularity results; the (OSM) regularity remains unproven.
